title: Select the freeze period for schema changes around the cutover
summary: A schema change during replication can stop the CDC link. The plan recommends a full freeze from the start of the copy to the end of the rollback window: 12 days.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: The CDC tool maps each MySQL column to a PostgreSQL column. If a team changes the schema on one side only, the mapping breaks and the replication stops.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [TESTED] In staging, the CDC tool stopped when I added a column on MySQL only. [src: report.md]
  • [READ] The team merged 9 schema changes in the last 90 days, about 0.7 per week. [src: report.md]
  • [READ] The peak freeze already blocks all production changes from 20 November 2026 to 4 January 2027. [src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html: With option a, teams cannot change the schema from 20 November to 17 January. About 1–2 planned changes move to after 17 January. [INFERRED]

options.label: Full freeze from the start of the copy to the end of the rollback window
options.detail_html: Dates: 5–17 January 2027 (12 days), with D3 option b. Cost: about 1–2 schema changes wait. Risk: low.

options.label: Short freeze from 1 day before to 2 days after the cutover
options.detail_html: Dates: 9–12 January 2027 (3 days). Outside the freeze, each change must go to MySQL, to PostgreSQL and to the CDC mapping in one release. Risk: medium. One missed step stops the replication.

options.label: No freeze, with a dual-apply procedure for each change
options.detail_html: Effort: 2 more days to write and test the procedure. Each change needs two reviewers. Risk: high, most of all on the night of the cutover.

recommendation_html: Option a. It delays only 1–2 changes. It removes the most common cause of a stopped replication.
